newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed, more churning seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed, more churning seen.

text.p: U.S. shares were little changed in quiet London trading on Thursday after the third consecutive fall on Wall Street overnight, dealers said. The Dow finished over 25 points at 6,036.46 as profit-taking again hit shares. Earlier in the session the index had tumbled nearly 70 points before technology stocks rebounded, helping cut losses.
"It's very, very quiet today," said one London trader.
"We're still looking for a bit more churning and profit- taking before the upward trend continues, but we've no long term worries about the market."

Among individual movers in London, General Motors added $1/4 to $54-3/4, after workers in Canada ended a 20-day strike by ratifying a tentative labour agreement between GM and the Canadian Auto Workers union.
Anheuser-Busch rose $1/4 to $39-3/8 following a bullish statement with third quarter earnings.
Elsewhere interest was thin, said dealers.
U.S. weekly jobless claims for the week ending October 19 are due at 1230 GMT, while on Friday U.S. September durable goods and existing home sales data are due.
